reviewFindings.detail: One Python standard-library artifact detects Termux, Windows, WSL, Linux, and macOS. It does not use ChatGPT browser orchestration.
No network command listener is created. Jobs enter through an owner-local filesystem queue. POSIX installation refuses root.
Commands are stored and executed as argv arrays with shell=False semantics. Model output is returned as data and is never executed.
Deterministic command jobs remain callable with no model and no cloud token. Prompt jobs use only loopback llama.cpp or Ollama and fail explicitly when neither is callable.

The artifact installs a stable fortress command, dedicated state/history/receipts, restart/status/doctor/sync surfaces, atomic queue claims, bounded exponential retries, tmux use where present, and platform persistence definitions.
The active checkout is not reset or replaced. Fortress owns a dedicated runtime clone, refuses dirty-runtime mutation, and permits only fast-forward synchronization.

Termux starts the existing Vlad swarm daemon only when the dedicated Home Center runtime, rish, and the daemon body are actually present. Absence is reported as unavailable rather than laundered as success.
Battery/charging-slope scaling is recorded but disabled exactly as ordered. Worker counts do not depend on battery in this slice.

knownEvidenceGaps: No command in this review ran on Drew's physical Android phone.
No command in this review ran on Drew's physical desktop.
Termux:Boot, systemd user services, launchd, and Windows Task Scheduler were rendered in isolation but not accepted on their real platforms.
The bootstrap detects existing loopback llama.cpp or Ollama; it does not claim a model is installed or callable on either machine.
Owner-local permissions are best-effort through each OS user boundary; this does not claim whole-OS hardening or root ownership.
The installed command directory may need to be added to PATH on a desktop shell; the installer reports its exact path.
